newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-India aluminium demand seen rising to 2000.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-India aluminium demand seen rising to 2000.

text.p: Consumption of aluminium in India is forecast to rise in step with growth in industrial production to 2000, the Macquarie Bank group said on Thursday.

"With industrial production forecast to average 5.5 percent to 6.0 percent between 1995 and 2000, flat intensity of use would imply an increase in aluminium demand from 572,000 tonnes to 765,000 tonnes by 2000," Jim Lennon, an analyst for Macquarie told the Australian Metals Conference here.
A more realistic forecast of growth of 7.0 percent annually would see India's aluminium demand grow to 800,000 tonnes by the end of the decade, Lennon added.
Aluminium is making strides into the building and construction sectors in doors, window frames and curtain walling applications, Lennon said.
"Timber is in increasingly short supply in India due to dwindling forest reserves and increasing environmental concerns," he said.
The Indian aluminium group Hindalco expects growth in aluminium consumption of around 15 percent a year in these sectors, Lennon said.
Demand from the consumer durables sector will also show strong growth as increasing incomes raise demand for a wide range of white goods, he said.
The electrical sector is currently the biggest user of aluminium, acounting for between 35 percent and 40 percent of domestic demand, Lennon said.
"However, even in this sector further strong growth is projected," lennon said.
Continuing rural electrification as well as several planned power projects will drive further aluminium demand, particularly for transmission cable, he said.
India's aluminium consumption grew at an annual rate of 5.7 percent between 1990 and 1995, Lennon said.
